doc.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
doc.interviewee: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor

title: Coleman Hawkins arriving in Chicago and as a creator
summary: Brown recalls Hawkins coming to Chicago, possibly earlier with Mamie Smith, and calls him the number one saxophonist and a creator like Louis and Duke.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Where has Hawkins been in? He was around Chicago for about a while.

Well he just came here with Fletcher's band. Well I think he was here even earlier maybe with Mamey Smith. Yes he did, he used to be a violin player. Years ago he started on violin, that's why he got to be a saxophone player. He came here with Mamey Smith and played in the grand theater.
Did he play violin with Mamey Smith? I don't think he did. I had an idea. Yeah, yeah.

Well Hawkins, like Duke, like Louis, a creator. And I always say that the imitators never, never greatest creators. To me Hawkins would always be the number one man. To me. A lot of those would come over and play a lot. A lot of those might blow Louis up. I mean Louis is still the king of that style. He's the creator. Hawkins was the creator of that fine saxophone player. A lot of them got a lot of good ones. But to me Hawkins has always number one. Always will be with Mamey.
